li.label: news from the road
li.description: A visitor told me who's at war, who's sick and what salt costs now. The world is still out there, being terrible without us.

li.label: tales of a famous blade
li.description: There's a duelist out there who can cut a candle in half without tipping it over. I'm going to need more candles.

li.label: swapped recipes
li.description: A traveler and I traded kitchen secrets. I came out ahead. So did the stew.

li.label: a stranger admired my work
li.description: Someone who has seen a hundred walls stopped to look at mine. Didn't have to. Did.

li.label: my work moved a stranger
li.description: A stranger went quiet in front of something I made. That's the whole reason to make anything.

li.label: a friend from the road
li.description: I made a friend from the caravan. We have a secret, a password and a frog funeral to our names.

li.label: songs by the fire
li.description: A traveler sang by the fire last night. The chorus is still stuck in my head, and I don't mind.

li.label: flirted with a visitor
li.description: Someone from the road laughed at my jokes and sat too close. I'm going to be thinking about that for a while.

li.label: they've heard of me
li.description: A stranger knew my name before I said it. There are stories about me on the road. Some of them might even be true.

li.label: a stranger's thanks
li.description: I did a small kindness for a traveler, and they paid it back in silver and herbs. People can still surprise you.

li.label: a stranger's dog
li.description: A visitor's dog leaned against my legs all afternoon. Best company I've had all week.

li.label: dice with a stranger
li.description: Played dice with a traveler all evening, for pebbles. Lost, won, lost again. Didn't think about raiders once.

li.label: insufferable outsider
li.description: Walked up to our gate and told us how to live. Next time they can tell it to the wall.

li.label: a fellow fighter
li.description: We've stood in the same kind of line and lost the same kind of friends. It doesn't need saying.

li.label: stared at me all day
li.description: Everywhere I went, those eyes. Never once said what they wanted.

li.label: good company
li.description: Made a long stop on a long road feel shorter.

li.label: flirted with me
li.description: Terrible jokes, nice laugh. I'll be thinking about that one on the road.

li.label: rude host
li.description: Insulted me at their own gate. I'll remember the face.

li.label: kind to me when I needed it
li.description: They didn't have to be kind to me. They were anyway.

li.label: out-haggled a trader
li.description: I talked a professional trader down to almost nothing. They called me a bandit. I've never been prouder.

li.label: drove a hard bargain
li.description: Robbed me blind with a straight face. I almost respect it. No, I do respect it.

li.label: haggled badly
li.description: I thought I'd driven a hard bargain. Then I saw what everyone else paid.

li.label: wanderlust
li.description: The trader talked about a warm sea and a city with a thousand chimneys. I keep looking at the road.

li.label: cheated me
li.description: Sold me rubbish and smiled while doing it. From now on I check the scales myself.

li.label: my work is known on the road
li.description: A trader recognized something I made. My work has been places I've never seen, and people pay good silver for it.

li.label: caravan gossip
li.description: The trader told me who's broke, who's feuding and who ate their trader. We're doing fine, by comparison.

li.label: a free taste
li.description: The trader let me taste something from very far away. I'm still thinking about it.

li.label: a taste of somewhere else
li.description: One pinch of something from three weeks south, and now everything we cook tastes like a lie. Worth it.

li.label: treats me like furniture
li.description: Snaps fingers at me, sent the soup back twice and has never once used my name.

li.label: noticed by a noble
li.description: Someone with a title said I'd do well at court. I don't know what a court is for, but apparently I'd do well at it.

li.label: a guest's thanks
li.description: I gave a frightened guest a bowl of stew and a blanket, and they thanked me like I'd saved their life. Maybe I did.

li.label: the guest pitched in
li.description: Our guest got tired of being protected and picked up an axe. Good help is hard to find, and this help was free.

li.label: a hunted guest
li.description: We're sheltering someone with killers on their trail. Every noise at night is them, until it isn't.

li.label: kept watch for a guest
li.description: Our guest was too scared to sleep, so I stayed up too. Somebody should be awake with them.

li.label: kind words through a door
li.description: I talked to a prisoner like a person today. They talked back like one.

li.label: taunted me through the door
li.description: Locked up and still found a way under my skin. I checked the walls twice because of them.

li.label: their story stays with me
li.description: They told me how they ended up raiding. I wish they hadn't. I wish I didn't understand it.

li.label: came from the same place
li.description: Same mud, same bread, same songs. Different side of the door, that's all.

li.label: face to face with them
li.description: I stood at the door and looked at the one who hurt me. They're the one locked in. Somehow I'm the one who can't breathe.

li.label: stared them down
li.description: The one who hurt me looked up, saw me, and looked away first. I've been waiting a long time for that.

li.label: insulted my cooking
li.description: Ate every crumb and then called it slop. From a cell. Fed by me.

li.label: a buried stash, supposedly
li.description: A prisoner told me where a chest of silver is buried. It's almost certainly a lie. Almost.

li.label: tried to bribe me
li.description: Offered me buried treasure for a key. Do I look that stupid? Don't answer that.

li.label: an enemy begged me
li.description: A downed raider begged me not to leave them out there. I can still feel the hand on my ankle.

li.label: cursed from the dirt
li.description: A raider who couldn't even stand spent their breath cursing me. My mother, my face, my colony. Thorough.

li.label: gave water to an enemy
li.description: A raider asked for water and I gave it. They came here to kill us. It still felt right.

li.label: an enemy's prayer
li.description: A fallen raider prayed in the mud to a god I don't know. I keep hearing the words.

li.label: a name to carry
li.description: A raider who thought they were dying gave me a name and a message. Now I'm carrying it, and I don't know where to.

li.label: spat on a raider
li.description: They came over our wall to kill us. Now they're in the dirt and I'm not, and I made sure they knew it.

li.label: spat on a helpless enemy
li.description: They were down and bleeding and couldn't lift a hand. Whatever they did, that wasn't right.

li.label: spat on me when I was down
li.description: I was on the ground, bleeding, and they spat on me. I won't forget it.

li.label: a farewell, postponed
li.description: A raider gave me a whole deathbed speech over a sprained ankle. I laughed about it all evening.
